nodes.description: Long-chain fatty-acid oxidation appears impaired, but the data point to two different sites. The 2018 dried-blood-spot profiles of the index patients showed low long-chain acylcarnitines (C16, C18) with a raised C0/(C16+C18) ratio, resembling CPT1 deficiency. That fits the authors' proposal that less cytosolic CoA means fewer activated long-chain acyl-CoAs. In contrast, the 2025 table records acylcarnitines as elevated in six patients. During crises F1:II and F4:II showed a VLCADD-like C14:1/C14:2 pattern, elevated long-chain acyl species and dicarboxylic aciduria, which suggests a block downstream of activation. Against a fixed systemic defect, the fasting respiratory quotient in two family B siblings was consistent with normal fat oxidation, and acylcarnitines were normal when patients were well. Acyl-CoA pools and fatty-acid flux have not been measured in patient cells or heart.

nodes.description: Oral pantethine enters the CoA pathway downstream of PPCS and so bypasses the defective step. It has been given as compassionate treatment to four patients at about 10-24 mg/kg/day. Family B siblings started it as adolescents and adults after cardiac damage. One improved (EF 36% to 48%) and the other stayed stable; the 2018 authors saw no significant clinical improvement. F6:IV.1 died at 21 of SARS-CoV-2 complications after four years on pantethine, with cardiac function reported stable through the infection. F1:II has had no rhabdomyolysis since starting it and has low-normal LV function. F5:IV.1 recovered full LV function, but she was also on a beta-blocker and ACE inhibitor and had an ICD. After starting pantethine, F1:II began excreting 3-methylcrotonylglycine; he carries a homozygous MCCC1 variant of uncertain significance, and the significance of this is unclear. No controlled data exist, and every treated patient also received standard care, so benefit cannot be attributed to pantethine alone. In vitro, pantethine raises CoA in patient cells and partly rescues cardiomyocyte phenotypes. It also rescues viability in dPPCS hypomorph flies.

nodes.description: Homozygous hypomorphic dPPCS flies have reduced viability. Their pre-pupal hearts show higher heart rate and arrhythmia index, more wall shortening and shorter systolic length. Dietary pantethine rescues viability; vitamin B5 was used as a control. Null dPPCS alleles are lethal at the first larval instar. The allele is not a patient allele, and fly CoA levels were not reported in this study.
